name: Hydrogen Gas Production
miniText: NetLogo Hydrogen Gas Production investigates how a surface reaction converts reactants into a gas with visible pressure effects. Hydronium ions encounter stationary zinc, producing hydrogen and dissolved zinc ions; escaping hydrogen particles collide within an expanding balloon representation. Provides the stochastic chemical-reaction perspective for finite particle counts, rather than an assertion that this spatial model uses the same algorithm [1]. Supplies the kinetic collision framework behind gas pressure [2]. Provides the temperature-dependent reaction-rate perspective needed to distinguish stoichiometry from calibrated reaction kinetics [3]. The source explicitly describes balloon mechanics as approximate; chloride is implicit and the few simulated molecules exaggerate fluctuations. The simulation illustrates limiting reactants, reaction location and the distinction between molecular events and macroscopic gas behavior. Reproducing these patterns establishes rule fidelity, not empirical validation.
